reviewerErrorAtV2.disclosure: I accepted v2 at 0 and 0. Codex found DR117N-V2-SF1 and was right: v2 said nothing about what recording it would do to D-056 eligibility.
reviewerErrorAtV2.whatIMissed: Naming EE-6b, EE-7c and EE-7e at G09/G14/G16 is the act that completes DR-117's remainder coverage. After D-157 and D-158, those three were the only EE classes left unnamed. Recording this candidate therefore flips D-056 gates 2 and 3 from not-holding to holding for DR-117 — the exact thing D-158 item 6 had said did not hold, and for exactly the reason it gave. v2 stated the condition-4 effect but was silent on the eligibility effect, and I cleared it.
reviewerErrorAtV2.mechanism: Both of my misses in this chain have the same shape. At D-157 turn 1 I checked what the row said and not what v1-slice's second limb required it to say. Here I checked every claim v2 made against live bytes and did not ask what v2 omitted about downstream standing. Verifying assertions is not the same as auditing for silence, and a naming act's whole significance can sit in the sentence it does not write.
reviewerErrorAtV2.correctionNow: I derived the eligibility effect myself from D-056's gate text and the live rows before reading v3's version of it, so that I was checking v3's statement rather than adopting it.

consideredAndDeclined.item: Forward note for the coordinator, not a finding: D-137's express reservation states its own ground
consideredAndDeclined.observation: D-137 reserved Class A because 'most enforcement classes are candidate-owned with no exact DR-G obligation'. That ground is precisely what D-157, D-158 and this naming have been curing — after this candidate, every one of the fourteen EE classes sits at an exact DR-G obligation with an owner. Whether a reservation survives the disappearance of its stated ground is a real question, and it is the question the next act in this chain will have to face.
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: It is not a defect in this artifact, which resolves the point in the conservative direction by holding gate 1 false and claiming less eligibility rather than more. Charging it would penalise the safe reading. I record it so the coordinator sees where the live question now sits.

consideredAndDeclined.item: The artifact carries no condition-2 effect statement and no reversibility clause, where the v6 predecessor template has the latter
consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: Condition 2 counts SATISFIED rows and nothing here is marked SATISFIED, so the effect is zero and no template in this corpus requires stating it. On reversibility I declined the same point at v1 on the ground that requiring v6's full shape for a three-gate amendment would be template worship; raising it now, after passing it at v1 and v2, would be moving the goalposts against a candidate that has answered every finding put to it.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Thirteen attacks run, none landed. Read the disclosure first: I accepted v2 at 0 and 0, and Codex was right that it was silent on eligibility. Naming EE-6b, EE-7c and EE-7e is the act that completes DR-117's remainder coverage, so recording it flips D-056 gates 2 and 3 to holding — the very thing D-158 item 6 denied while those three were unnamed — and v2 never said so. Both of my misses in this chain share a shape: I check what an artifact asserts and not what its silence conceals about downstream standing. So this time I derived the eligibility effect myself from D-056's gate text and the live rows before reading v3's version of it. It is accurate. I enumerated v5's fourteen EE classes against live bytes: G29 names seven, G30 names three, this candidate names three, the join discharges EE-3a, and the union is exactly the fourteen with every owning gate carrying an owner — so gates 2 and 3 would hold. Gate 1 is correctly held false, and D-137's adopted text does carry the express reservation cited, saying in terms that Class A is not opened. The new field then refuses eligible-in-kind, SATISFY, Class A and the D-096 grant, and closes with 'this file existing is not that recording'. Custody and mechanics are clean: v3 at fb5e9284 and frozen v2 at 8c051860 both unmoved, HEAD 0fcf3d3, file 08 3a9442d1, DR-117 still OPEN, all eleven digests reproduce, and all nine verbatim quotations still compare byte-exact against the current register. The change is strictly additive — one key added, none removed, all three gate objects field-for-field identical to v2, condition4Effect and doesNot byte-identical, and the remeasurement clause gaining only the v2 operand. One forward note, recorded as an observation rather than charged: D-137 grounded its reservation in most enforcement classes being candidate-owned with no exact DR-G obligation, and that ground is exactly what this chain has now cured. Whether a reservation outlives its stated ground is the question the next act will face; this artifact resolves it conservatively by claiming less, which is why it is not a finding here. Finally, the split on this candidate has run both ways — Codex accepted v1 where I rejected it, and rejected v2 where I accepted it. Both objections were sound. Neither reviewer alone would have produced v3.
